organization.name: Centene Corporation
organization.short_description: Centene Corporation is a leading multi-national healthcare enterprise that provides programs and services to under-insured and uninsured individuals. As the largest Medicaid managed care organization in the US, Centene serves over 28 million members across all 50 states.

contactAnalysis.name: Kevin Basco
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Information Officer
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CIO overseeing $1.2B technology modernization across 50-state Medicaid operations — approves all enterprise AI platform investments at this scale.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Present business case after champion-building phase. Focus on $1.2B tech modernization alignment and enterprise-scale ROI.

contactAnalysis.name: Shannon Eusey
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Data & Analytics Officer
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CDAO owns the data strategy and analytics platform — direct decision-maker for AI/ML tooling and data infrastructure.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Engage with data architecture vision showing how AI accelerates their enterprise data lake migration and analytics modernization.

contactAnalysis.name: Drew Blossman
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Digital Transformation & Innovation
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Leads digital transformation initiatives — would champion AI tools that accelerate innovation roadmap and member experience.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: First touch target. Reference AI Center of Excellence and $1.2B tech modernization — offer complimentary use case assessment.

contactAnalysis.name: Maria Santos
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Member Services & Contact Center
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Runs Centene's 15,000-agent contact center handling 100M+ annual member calls across 50 states — the single largest cost center that conversational AI transforms.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Lead with call center pain: real-time agent assist, call summarization, after-call work elimination. This is where OpenAI's ROI hits fastest.

contactAnalysis.name: Jennifer Martinez
contactAnalysis.title: Director, Clinical Informatics
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Clinical informatics director evaluates AI solutions for clinical use cases and care delivery workflow alignment.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Demonstrate clinical AI applications for Medicaid care management — prior auth automation and care gap closure.

contactAnalysis.name: David Park
contactAnalysis.title: Director, Data Science & Machine Learning
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Leads data science team — would technically evaluate AI capabilities, model performance, and integration requirements.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Technical validation session. Show how platform accelerates their team's work rather than replacing it.

contactAnalysis.name: Lisa Thompson
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Information Security & Compliance
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Security & compliance VP will scrutinize HIPAA compliance, data handling, and security posture for 28M+ member PHI.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Proactively share SOC 2, HITRUST, and BAA documentation. Address multi-state Medicaid compliance requirements upfront.

contactAnalysis.name: Michael Russo
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Procurement & Vendor Management
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Controls vendor selection and contract negotiation — can slow deals through procurement processes and existing vendor preferences.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Engage early with pricing framework and vendor qualification materials. Understand existing vendor landscape to position as complement.

plan.executiveSummary: Centene Corporation is a Tier 1 strategic account — the nation's largest Medicaid managed care organization with 28M+ members, $154B revenue, and a $1.2B technology modernization initiative actively being deployed. Their AI Center of Excellence and CEO's 'AI-first approach to member experience' signal executive commitment and allocated budget. Even a modest initial deployment at Centene's scale represents significant ACV with clear expansion potential across business units.
plan.painToProductFit:
1. CLAIMS PROCESSING VOLUME: Hundreds of millions of claims annually — AI automation reduces manual review rates, accelerates adjudication, and improves accuracy.
2. MEMBER EXPERIENCE AT SCALE: 28M+ members, many in underserved populations, need multilingual, accessible AI-powered communication tools.
3. PROVIDER NETWORK MANAGEMENT: Prior authorization, network adequacy analysis, and provider communication across hundreds of thousands of providers.
4. FRAUD, WASTE, AND ABUSE: AI detection improving catch rate on $154B claims portfolio = billions in potential recovery.
plan.competitiveThreats: OPTUM/UHG: Analytics services with deep payer expertise — likely existing relationship. IBM WATSON HEALTH: Historical healthcare AI presence. COGNIZANT: IT services provider with healthcare practice. ALTERNATIVE PLATFORMS: Google Cloud Healthcare API, Azure AI for Health, AWS HealthLake competing for infrastructure. INTERNAL BUILD: 20+ data scientists with existing Kubernetes ML platform.
plan.timingUrgency: $1.2B tech modernization budget being allocated in phases — getting in during planning cycle is critical. New CDAO and VP of Digital Transformation are establishing their technology stack. CMS interoperability mandates and Medicaid unwinding require new capabilities by specific deadlines. UnitedHealth and Elevance both publicizing AI investments — Centene can't afford to fall behind.
plan.dealStrategy: Champion-led enterprise entry over 3-6 months. Phase 1: Enter through Drew Blossman (VP Digital Transformation) with reference to AI Center of Excellence and tech modernization. Phase 2: Technical validation with Robert Chen (Enterprise Architecture) and David Park (Data Science). Phase 3: Present business case to Kevin Basco (CIO) and Shannon Eusey (CDAO). Phase 4: Proactively address Lisa Thompson's security concerns. Phase 5: Pilot in single state (Texas Medicaid). Estimated deal size: $1-3M initial, $15M+ enterprise. Risks: strong internal team, 50-state regulatory complexity, rigorous procurement.
plan.discoveryQuestions:
1. How is the AI Center of Excellence structured, and what are its top 3 priorities this year?
2. What percentage of claims still require manual review, and what's the cost per manual review?
3. How are you handling member communication across languages and literacy levels?
4. Where in the $1.2B tech modernization is AI/analytics prioritized — what's funded vs. still in planning?
5. What's your timeline for the enterprise data lake migration, and how does AI fit into that architecture?
plan.roiFramework: Claims automation: Reducing manual review from 30% to 15% across ~500M annual claims at $3-5/review = $225-375M annual savings. Member services automation: AI handling 40% of 50M annual routine inquiries = $300-500M savings. Fraud/waste/abuse: 2% improvement in catch rate on $154B claims = $3.08B additional recovery. PILOT: 90-day pilot in single state (Texas Medicaid), one claims category, target 50% reduction in manual reviews with 3x ROI.
